Messages.Author: Ramsteiner
Messages.Body:
Talking with a fellow Methuselah on interesting combos has brought
this question forward.

When does the Malkavian Rider Clause vote have to be called? The next
turn the Malkavian player starts? Or can it be held until the
Malkavian player is ready to call a vote (possibly a few turns in the
future)?

Additionally, can Malkavian Rider Clauses be "stored"? (i.e. having
them stack up due to a high quantity of votes being called on the
table) If they can be stored, are all of them used up on the next vote
that is called or can they be used to pass separate individual votes
from the Malkavian player?

Michael Eichler
Prince of Ramstein

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Ramsteiner <ramst...@my-deja.com> wrote:
> When does the Malkavian Rider Clause vote have to be called? The next
> turn the Malkavian player starts? Or can it be held until the
> Malkavian player is ready to call a vote (possibly a few turns in the
> future)?

Held indefinitely.

> Additionally, can Malkavian Rider Clauses be "stored"? (i.e. having
> them stack up due to a high quantity of votes being called on the
> table) If they can be stored, are all of them used up on the next vote
> that is called or can they be used to pass separate individual votes
> from the Malkavian player?

They would all be "used up" in making the next referendum you call
pass.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Ramsteiner wrote:
> LSJ <vte...@white-wolf.com> wrote:
> > Ramsteiner <ramst...@my-deja.com> wrote:
> > > Additionally, can Malkavian Rider Clauses be "stored"?

> > They would all be "used up" in making the next referendum you call
> > pass.
> >
> I can see the "logic" for all of them being used up on the next
> referendum called, however, each are individual reaction cards that
> occurred at different times. But with Anarch Revolt, you have to call
> separate votes to remove each copy of the card in play. Why wouldn't
> just one vote do it all for all copies then?

Card text.

MRCs say that they make the "next" vote pass. So, after (redundantly)
making the next vote pass, their effects are ended.

AR is burned by a vote. It doesn't say "All AR in play can be burned by a
vote", but just that "this card" can be.
